subject: Re: Request for cross-border transfer evidence and DPA annex items
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@healthbridge.com>

Date: 2027-05-20T16:12:00Z
Subject: Cross-border transfer evidence needed for RFP - Section 5

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our procurement and privacy teams are moving through the RFP and have a few follow-up asks specific to Section 5 (data transfers / international safeguards). Can you provide the following items by EOD Thursday if possible?

- Confirmation of lawful basis for EU->US processing for log/telemetry data and embeddings
- DPF/adequacy-related mapping and any supplementary controls you rely on
- A copy of the EU SCCs + your proposed DPA annex language (redlines or example annex)
- Current subprocessor list and whether any subprocessor processes in APAC/Japan
- High-level data flow diagram showing where customer PII/embeddings transit and persist
- SOC 2 or other independent attestations covering production inference service

I've attached a short spreadsheet (HealthBridge_RFP_Section5.xls) with checkboxes to help track items.

If anything is out of scope we can flag it, but we need to capture what evidence you can provide for our privacy review.

Best,
Sophie Turner
Head of Privacy, HealthBridge
Sophie Turner | HealthBridge

Date: 2027-05-21T02:16:00Z
Subject: Dataflow, subprocessors, and mapping for HealthBridge RFP

Jordan / Monica — attaching the technical artifacts requested for HealthBridge Section 5. Highlights below.

Attachments included: redwood_dpf_mapping_v2.xlsx; subprocessor_list.csv; redwood_dataflow_v1.png (see Drive link in final package).

Summary:
- Lawful basis: customer-directed processing (contract + performance) for embeddings and telemetry; we support legitimate interests for platform operational metrics with documentation per client preference.
- Embeddings: by default, embeddings produced via the hosted API are not stored persistently unless the customer opts in; when stored, they are encrypted at rest and retention is configurable per customer.
- KV cache: ephemeral and resident only for the lifetime of the inference session; not written to durable storage.
- Cross-border: inference requests may route to US-hosted inference pools for certain model families. For EU customers requiring EU-only processing we offer Private (VPC) deployments and region pinning.
- Subprocessors: list attached. Notable: public cloud (us-west) provider for managed infra, monitoring vendor (EU region available), and a vector store partner (optional). APAC/Japan processing is only used in private deployments or specifically contracted deployments.

If you need a higher-detail packet (raw logs, sample retention configs), tell me which specific items and I can redact and provide.

Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpf_mapping_v2.xlsx; subprocessor_list.csv

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Cross-border transfer evidence needed for RFP - Section 5

Hi Sophie — following up with legal/contract input.

- We use the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as the baseline for EU->US transfers and include a DPA annex that reflects our technical and organizational controls.
- I've drafted a proposed annex (dpa_annex_draft.docx) that maps the controls in your checklist to our operational procedures. The draft includes a short section on transfer risk mitigation and optional commitments for Customer-specific region pinning.
- SOC 2 Type II: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for our inference platform; I attached the summary (SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf). Full attestations can be shared under NDA.

Two small asks:
1) Please confirm whether HealthBridge requires formal DPF assessment outputs (a named DPF/contractual scheme) or if a controls-based mapping + SCCs is sufficient.
2) If HealthBridge has a preferred DPA Annex template (you mentioned an in-house annex during the RFP kickoff), share it and we will align redlines.

Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa_annex_draft.docx; SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf

Subject: Consolidated package: cross-border mapping, DPA annex draft, and attestations (HealthBridge RFP HB-2247)

Sophie — thanks for your patience. Attached and linked below is the consolidated evidence package for Section 5. Summary of what we've provided and next steps: 

Package contents (attachments and Drive):
- redwood_dpf_mapping_v2.xlsx — control mapping and transfer risk annotations
- subprocessor_list.csv — current subprocessor roster with region column
- dpa_annex_draft.docx — proposed DPA annex (tracks SCCs + optional region-pinning clause)
- SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf — high-level attestation summary
- Redwood_Drive_Link.txt — link to a Drive folder with the full dataflow diagram (redwood_dataflow_v1.png) and an exportable retention policy template

Responses to your checklist:
- Lawful basis: contract (processing necessary for performance) for customer data; optional legitimate interest for operational telemetry with documented DPIA when used.
- DPF/adequacy: we provide a controls-based mapping; if HealthBridge requires a formal DPF attestation we can discuss scope and timeline.
- EU SCCs + Annex: attached draft annex is based on SCCs; Monica has redlined optional language for region pinning.
- Subprocessors: attached; we commit to 30 days notice before adding a new subprocessor unless contractually negotiated otherwise.
- Data flow: see Drive (redwood_dataflow_v1.png) — primary transit is encrypted TLS to US-hosted inference pools; embeddings storage is opt-in and encrypted at rest.
- SOC 2: summary attached; full report available under NDA.

Next steps:
1) Sophie — please confirm whether the draft annex aligns with HealthBridge's template or share your annex and we'll apply redlines (Monica will handle).
2) If you'd like a short walkthrough of the Drive artifacts, I'm happy to set a 30-minute call this week.
